title: GraphQL Schema & Types
description: Learn the fundamentals of GraphQL types and schema definitions

questions.explanation: A GraphQL type describes the shape of data - the fields it contains and their data types.
acceptable_answers: a way to define the shape of data
questions.hint: Think about how you describe what data looks like

questions.text: What is the purpose of a GraphQL schema?
questions.explanation: A schema defines all possible types and how they relate to each other, forming the contract between client and server.
questions.hint: It's like a blueprint of your API

questions.text: What are the three core types in GraphQL?
questions.explanation: Query (read data), Mutation (write data), and Subscription (real-time updates) are the three root types.
questions.hint: One is for reading, one for writing, one for live updates

questions.text: What does the exclamation mark (!) mean in GraphQL?
questions.explanation: The ! indicates a non-null field - it must always return a value and cannot be null.
questions.hint: It's about whether a field can be empty

questions.text: What is a scalar type in GraphQL?
questions.explanation: A scalar type is a basic type that represents a single value (like String, Int, Boolean, Float, ID).
acceptable_answers: a basic type for single values
primitive types like String and Int
